scenes.headline: How SteerDistill teaches a 4-bit agent its own fixes
scenes.sub: Steer the failing turn, check it by running it, then distill the hint away
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wilder! Today, a training method that keeps a four-bit agent close to its full-precision self, by making it fix its own mistakes.

scenes.title: Where the points go
scenes.sub: One wrong turn sinks a long task
scenes.say: Chapter one. Where the points go.

scenes.title: Why turns multiply
scenes.say: Start with a toy. Say each turn of a task goes right with probability p.

parts.note: p per turn, k turns, every one right
parts.say: If the task needs k turns and any wrong one sinks it, the task succeeds with p to the power k.

parts.note: a single-turn eval measures p, an agent eval this
parts.say: A single-turn benchmark measures p. An agent benchmark measures p to the k, so small losses per turn get multiplied.

steps.say: At ninety-nine percent per turn, twenty turns still succeed eighty-two percent of the time.
Drop to ninety-seven percent per turn. That is two points on a single question, and twenty-seven points at twenty turns.
This is my arithmetic, not the paper's. Real turns are not independent, but the shape holds.
The paper calls the first wrong turn a behavioral divergence. Asked to book a train with no route, the full-precision model asks where to.
On-Policy QAD invents a route from Boston to New York, and asks for tickets.
Plain GPTQ invents San Francisco to Los Angeles, then asks the user to confirm.

scenes.title: Steer, verify, keep
scenes.sub: A teacher's hint, checked by running it

scenes.text: Let the full-precision teacher hint at the failing turn, keep the student's own fix once running it checks out, then train the hint away.
scenes.say: Here's the idea. The full-precision teacher hints at the failing turn. The student writes its own fix, which is kept only if running it checks out. Then training removes the hint.

params.fkl: forward KL to the student with G
params.rkl: reverse KL to the BF16 teacher
legend: The first turn whose state change has no match
Restore the state, add a hint, retry
The retry moves the state like the reference
Then the student carries on alone
Each turn gets its own distillation target

steps.say: Here is a task as a row of turns. On top, the teacher's successful run. Below, the four-bit student, which parts ways where its action changes the environment differently.
steps.term: Divergence: first turn whose state change differs

steps.say: Restore everything before that turn. The teacher writes a steering prompt, and the student retries. This attempt fails the check, so the teacher refines the prompt.
The next attempt moves the environment exactly as the reference did. It passes local verification, and the fix is kept.
Then the student carries on with no prompt. If it slips again, the loop finds the next divergence.
Training uses both. At the corrected turn, the target is the student with the prompt. Everywhere else, the full-precision teacher.
In this training case, the student calls cat on a file from its home folder. The tool reads only the current directory, so it fails.

steps.term: Steering prompt: a rule, never the call
steps.say: The teacher's prompt gives a rule: navigate to the workspace directory before reading. It never writes the call itself.
From the restored state, the student checks where it is, changes directory, and reads the file.
The check compares the result with the reference. The directory moved the same way and the file text matches. Accepted.
In the released code, the database is saved before and after every turn. Both copies must match the reference's.
If the reference's turn changed the state, matching it is enough.
If it only read, the returned result must match too.

scenes.title: Training the hint away
scenes.say: Chapter three. Training the hint away.

scenes.title: Two targets, two directions
scenes.text: loss = KL(p_G || q) or KL(q || p_T)
scenes.say: The learner, q, sees the history with every prompt removed.

parts.note: corrected turns: copy the prompted student
parts.say: At a corrected turn it matches the frozen student that did see the prompt, with forward KL. So it learns to act as if the hint were there.

parts.note: every other turn: stay near the teacher
parts.say: Everywhere else it stays close to the full-precision teacher, with reverse KL. Swapping the two directions costs about two and a half points.

scenes.title: Does it hold up?
scenes.say: Chapter four. Does it hold up?

scenes.title: Qwen3-8B at W4A16, five-benchmark average
scenes.say: On Qwen three, eight billion, full precision averages fifty-three point five four. GPTQ, forty-six point three six. The best baseline, fifty-one. SteerDistill, fifty-three point one eight.

scenes.title: The loop, and what it costs

steps.say: The authors' own animation of the loop: guidance, retry, verification, and a refine arrow when the check fails.
Then the cost. Thirty-two GPU hours reach thirty-one point six eight percent on tau squared bench. The strongest baseline needs ninety-six hours to reach twenty-nine point eight four.

scenes.title: Where the claim bends
scenes.say: The one-point claim is true as stated. Here is where it bends.

items.say: It holds for the average. On Gemma, two benchmarks sit just over a point under full precision.
It holds at four-bit weights. With eight-bit activations the gap nears two points, and at two-bit weights it passes ten.

items.text: Needs a reference and state restore
items.say: And it needs a teacher that solves the task, and an environment you can snapshot and restore.
